blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.37
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.37

blocks.text: करणशक्तिः स्वतोऽनुभवात्
blocks.directed: [slowly] करणशक्तिः स्वतोऽनुभवात्

blocks.text: Karaṇaśaktiḥ svato ’nubhavāt.
blocks.directed: Karaṇaśaktiḥ svato ’nubhavāt.

blocks.text: The power of creation is known from one’s own experience.
blocks.directed: The power of creation is known from one’s own experience.

blocks.text: You Literally Generate Entire Worlds in Dreams. Śiva Would Like a Word.
blocks.directed: You Literally Generate Entire Worlds in Dreams. Śiva Would Like a Word.

blocks.text: Oh, this is a beauty.
blocks.directed: Oh, this is a beauty.

blocks.text: Because Kṣemarāja is about to support his metaphysical argument by appealing to something everyone can investigate.
blocks.directed: Because Kṣemarāja is about to support his metaphysical argument by appealing to something everyone can investigate.

blocks.text: Their own experience.
blocks.directed: Their own experience.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Karaṇa — making, producing, creating.
blocks.directed: Karaṇa — making, producing, creating.

blocks.text: Śakti — power.
blocks.directed: Śakti — power.

blocks.text: Svataḥ — from oneself, from one’s own standpoint.
blocks.directed: Svataḥ — from oneself, from one’s own standpoint.

blocks.text: Anubhavāt — from direct experience.
blocks.directed: Anubhavāt — from direct experience.

blocks.text: And the interpretation is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And the interpretation is:

blocks.text: The creative power of consciousness is already evident through experience.
blocks.directed: The creative power of consciousness is already evident through experience.

blocks.text: Now, Kṣemarāja gives two examples.
blocks.directed: Now, Kṣemarāja gives two examples.

blocks.text: Saṅkalpa.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Saṅkalpa.

blocks.text: Mental construction, imaginative determination.
blocks.directed: Mental construction, imaginative determination.

blocks.text: And:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And:

blocks.text: Svapna.
blocks.directed: Svapna.

blocks.text: Dreaming.
blocks.directed: Dreaming.

blocks.text: And this is where the whole thing becomes extraordinary.
blocks.directed: And this is where the whole thing becomes extraordinary.

blocks.text: Consider a dream.
blocks.directed: Consider a dream.

blocks.text: You’re asleep.
blocks.directed: You’re asleep.

blocks.text: And suddenly there’s a world.
blocks.directed: And suddenly there’s a world.

blocks.text: Buildings.
blocks.directed: Buildings.

blocks.text: People.
blocks.directed: People.

blocks.text: Mountains.
blocks.directed: Mountains.

blocks.text: An entire environment.
blocks.directed: An entire environment.

blocks.text: Perhaps you’re standing in a city you’ve never visited.
blocks.directed: Perhaps you’re standing in a city you’ve never visited.

blocks.text: Perhaps you’re speaking to somebody who died years ago.
blocks.directed: Perhaps you’re speaking to somebody who died years ago.

blocks.text: Perhaps you’re being chased by a six-foot goose wearing a police uniform.
blocks.directed: Perhaps you’re being chased by a six-foot goose wearing a police uniform.

blocks.text: Absolutely terrifying.
blocks.directed: Absolutely terrifying.

blocks.text: But for the duration of the dream, the world appears.
blocks.directed: But for the duration of the dream, the world appears.

blocks.text: You experience it.
blocks.directed: You experience it.

blocks.text: You respond to it.
blocks.directed: You respond to it.

blocks.text: You may even believe it’s entirely independent of you.
blocks.directed: You may even believe it’s entirely independent of you.

blocks.text: And then you wake up.
blocks.directed: And then you wake up.

blocks.text: And discover that the dream world was not an independently existing physical environment of the same kind as your waking surroundings.
blocks.directed: And discover that the dream world was not an independently existing physical environment of the same kind as your waking surroundings.

blocks.text: It arose through mental activity.
blocks.directed: It arose through mental activity.

blocks.text: Now, modern neuroscience and Trika metaphysics would explain this in very different ways.
blocks.directed: Now, modern neuroscience and Trika metaphysics would explain this in very different ways.

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja’s immediate point is about the experience of manifestation.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja’s immediate point is about the experience of manifestation.

blocks.text: The mind can present forms, objects and situations that are experienced as a world.
blocks.directed: The mind can present forms, objects and situations that are experienced as a world.

blocks.text: And this shows, within his argument, that consciousness possesses a power of presentation or manifestation.
blocks.directed: And this shows, within his argument, that consciousness possesses a power of presentation or manifestation.

blocks.text: He connects this with the Īśvarapratyabhijñā, whose account of knowledge and agency appeals to the capacity of living beings to manifest desired forms through cognition.
blocks.directed: He connects this with the Īśvarapratyabhijñā, whose account of knowledge and agency appeals to the capacity of living beings to manifest desired forms through cognition.

blocks.text: And this is one of the most fascinating connections in the entire work.
blocks.directed: And this is one of the most fascinating connections in the entire work.

blocks.text: Because the argument isn’t merely:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Because the argument isn’t merely:

blocks.text: “Imagine something, therefore you can physically create anything.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Imagine something, therefore you can physically create anything.”

blocks.text: That would be a logical leap.
blocks.directed: That would be a logical leap.

blocks.text: And a rather dangerous one if you were planning to manifest a helicopter.
blocks.directed: And a rather dangerous one if you were planning to manifest a helicopter.

blocks.text: The first step is more subtle.
blocks.directed: The first step is more subtle.

blocks.text: Experience already displays a power of conscious manifestation.
blocks.directed: Experience already displays a power of conscious manifestation.

blocks.text: In dreaming, the conscious field presents an elaborate world.
blocks.directed: In dreaming, the conscious field presents an elaborate world.

blocks.text: In imagination, objects can be mentally represented without their corresponding external presence.
blocks.directed: In imagination, objects can be mentally represented without their corresponding external presence.

blocks.text: And these examples become important for the Pratyabhijñā theory of agency.
blocks.directed: And these examples become important for the Pratyabhijñā theory of agency.

blocks.text: Now Kṣemarāja takes the argument further.
blocks.directed: Now Kṣemarāja takes the argument further.

blocks.text: He says that when this creative power is recognised with intense determination, it can, according to the tantric account, become capable of manifesting things beyond the private domain of imagination.
blocks.directed: He says that when this creative power is recognised with intense determination, it can, according to the tantric account, become capable of manifesting things beyond the private domain of imagination.

blocks.text: He even cites the Tattvagarbha on the yogi whose will becomes like a kalpavṛkṣa.
blocks.directed: He even cites the Tattvagarbha on the yogi whose will becomes like a kalpavṛkṣa.

blocks.text: The wish-fulfilling tree.
blocks.directed: The wish-fulfilling tree.

blocks.text: A tree that grants whatever you desire.
blocks.directed: A tree that grants whatever you desire.

blocks.text: Quite an improvement over ordinary gardening.
blocks.directed: Quite an improvement over ordinary gardening.

blocks.text: But again, distinguish the levels.
blocks.directed: But again, distinguish the levels.

blocks.text: The fact that dreams contain generated experiences is observable.
blocks.directed: The fact that dreams contain generated experiences is observable.

blocks.text: The conclusion that a yogi can therefore manifest public physical objects at will is an additional traditional claim, not something established by the dream example alone.
blocks.directed: The conclusion that a yogi can therefore manifest public physical objects at will is an additional traditional claim, not something established by the dream example alone.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja makes both moves, and we should preserve both without conflating them. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja makes both moves, and we should preserve both without conflating them. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now let’s explore the philosophical point more deeply.
blocks.directed: Now let’s explore the philosophical point more deeply.

blocks.text: Why does the dream matter so much to nondual Śaivism?
blocks.directed: Why does the dream matter so much to nondual Śaivism?

blocks.text: Because it destabilises an assumption we make constantly.
blocks.directed: Because it destabilises an assumption we make constantly.

blocks.text: That whatever appears to consciousness must be entirely independent of the conscious process through which it is experienced.
blocks.directed: That whatever appears to consciousness must be entirely independent of the conscious process through which it is experienced.

blocks.text: In a dream, that assumption becomes questionable.
blocks.directed: In a dream, that assumption becomes questionable.

blocks.text: A whole environment can appear as though it exists independently of the dreamer.
blocks.directed: A whole environment can appear as though it exists independently of the dreamer.

blocks.text: And yet its manifestation is tied to the dreaming condition.
blocks.directed: And yet its manifestation is tied to the dreaming condition.

blocks.text: Now, Kṣemarāja uses this to illustrate the larger doctrine of manifestation.
blocks.directed: Now, Kṣemarāja uses this to illustrate the larger doctrine of manifestation.

blocks.text: The waking universe, from the supreme standpoint of Trika, is also understood as an expression of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The waking universe, from the supreme standpoint of Trika, is also understood as an expression of consciousness.

blocks.text: But not simply a private dream produced by your personal human mind.
blocks.directed: But not simply a private dream produced by your personal human mind.

blocks.text: That distinction is absolutely essential.
blocks.directed: That distinction is absolutely essential.

blocks.text: Universal consciousness is not identical to the ordinary individual imagination.
blocks.directed: Universal consciousness is not identical to the ordinary individual imagination.

blocks.text: The supreme Aham is not the contracted ego.
blocks.directed: The supreme Aham is not the contracted ego.

blocks.text: And therefore Trika’s account of cosmic manifestation is not the claim that the world exists merely because your private personality imagines it.
blocks.directed: And therefore Trika’s account of cosmic manifestation is not the claim that the world exists merely because your private personality imagines it.

blocks.text: That would be a very crude form of solipsism.
blocks.directed: That would be a very crude form of solipsism.

blocks.text: The doctrine is more radical.
blocks.directed: The doctrine is more radical.

blocks.text: The individual mind itself is a manifestation within universal consciousness.
blocks.directed: The individual mind itself is a manifestation within universal consciousness.

blocks.text: And the world of waking experience is also understood through that universal conscious reality.
blocks.directed: And the world of waking experience is also understood through that universal conscious reality.

blocks.text: The individual doesn’t create Śiva.
blocks.directed: The individual doesn’t create Śiva.

blocks.text: Śiva manifests the individual.
blocks.directed: Śiva manifests the individual.

blocks.text: And the world.
blocks.directed: And the world.

blocks.text: And their relationship.
blocks.directed: And their relationship.

blocks.text: Now consider the beauty of that.
blocks.directed: Now consider the beauty of that.

blocks.text: Ordinarily you ask:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Ordinarily you ask:

blocks.text: “How does my consciousness relate to the world?”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “How does my consciousness relate to the world?”

blocks.text: But Trika changes the question.
blocks.directed: But Trika changes the question.

blocks.text: It asks:
blocks.directed: [short pause] It asks:

blocks.text: How does universal consciousness manifest the distinction between a limited subject and its world?
blocks.directed: How does universal consciousness manifest the distinction between a limited subject and its world?

blocks.text: The first question assumes two fundamental realities and tries to connect them.
blocks.directed: The first question assumes two fundamental realities and tries to connect them.

blocks.text: The second begins from one reality and explains the appearance of differentiation.
blocks.directed: The second begins from one reality and explains the appearance of differentiation.

blocks.text: And that is precisely what Kṣemarāja’s interpretation of karaṇaśakti is doing.
blocks.directed: And that is precisely what Kṣemarāja’s interpretation of karaṇaśakti is doing.

blocks.text: The creative power of consciousness is understood as intrinsic to the Self.
blocks.directed: The creative power of consciousness is understood as intrinsic to the Self.

blocks.text: And dreaming becomes one accessible illustration of manifestation.
blocks.directed: And dreaming becomes one accessible illustration of manifestation.

blocks.text: Now, this brings us to an enormous philosophical development.
blocks.directed: Now, this brings us to an enormous philosophical development.

blocks.text: Because the final sūtras are about to move away from the special question of extraordinary creative powers.
blocks.directed: Because the final sūtras are about to move away from the special question of extraordinary creative powers.

blocks.text: And return to something much more immediate.
blocks.directed: And return to something much more immediate.

blocks.text: The three fundamental movements of manifestation.
blocks.directed: The three fundamental movements of manifestation.

blocks.text: Arising.
blocks.directed: Arising.

blocks.text: Remaining.
blocks.directed: Remaining.

blocks.text: Subsiding.
blocks.directed: Subsiding.

blocks.text: And the fourth state of consciousness that underlies them.
blocks.directed: And the fourth state of consciousness that underlies them.

blocks.text: But this time, Kṣemarāja is going to connect them to everyday experiences of joy, delight, wonder, and even sensual pleasure.
blocks.directed: But this time, Kṣemarāja is going to connect them to everyday experiences of joy, delight, wonder, and even sensual pleasure.

blocks.text: Which is very tantric indeed.
blocks.directed: Which is very tantric indeed.

blocks.text: Apparently the highest metaphysical reality can become apparent while listening to beautiful music.
blocks.directed: Apparently the highest metaphysical reality can become apparent while listening to beautiful music.

blocks.text: Excellent.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Excellent.

blocks.text: Finally, a spiritual path with decent acoustics.
blocks.directed: Finally, a spiritual path with decent acoustics.
